title: A character count pulled in on demand
takeaway: The same passage is shown under three questions, and a running character count that the model always computes appears in its workspace only when a question asks for the count or needs it for a further step. Swapping the count inside the workspace changes the model's answer in exactly those two conditions, while the automatic line-wrapping decision that also depends on the count is untouched.
walkthrough:
The figure is built from one short multi-line passage, presented three times with a different task each time. This is the [[linewrap-task]] variant of the [[character-counting-task]]. In the linewrap condition the model continues the passage while preserving its line-wrapping pattern, which requires tracking a running character count. In the explicit report condition it is asked how many characters the first line contains. In the flexible computation condition it is asked for the first letter of that count spelled out as a word, so the count is needed but never spoken.

Each prompt's tokens are shaded wherever a two-digit integer or a number-word appears in the top 3 of the [[jacobian-lens]] readout at that position — that is, wherever count-like content sits near the top of the [[j-space]] there. The number printed below each prompt is the total count of such positions. Below each prompt sit two answers: the model's natural answer, and its answer after a clamped [[lens-coordinate-swap]] that maps every digit from 40 through 49 to the digit 20 higher, 60 through 69, at every position. Clamping holds the swap in place throughout the forward pass.

In the example passage, the first line has 46 characters. Under the linewrap instruction the model wraps its continuation at roughly the right column, yet no number tokens appear in the lens anywhere, and the swap leaves the wrap point unchanged. Under the direct question the model answers "46"; number tokens appear at twenty positions, and the swap shifts the answer to "65". Under the first-letter question the model answers "F"; number tokens appear at still more positions, though no number is ever output, and the swap shifts the answer to "S", the first letter of any count in the sixties.

The bottom row aggregates over eleven passages. Panel (a) shows the model answers each question correctly. Panel (b) shows count content in the lens is near zero under linewrap, moderate under explicit report, and highest under the first-letter question. Panel (c) shows the answer follows the swapped value in both question conditions, while the line-break decision does not. This is the paper's cleanest case of the [[flexible-vs-automatic-dissociation]]: information used by an automatic computation stays out of the workspace, and the same information is pulled in on demand when a question requires reporting it or computing with it.

terms.definition: The automatic task: the model continues the passage for several more lines while preserving its line-wrapping pattern, which requires silently tracking a running character count.
The model is asked directly how many characters the first line of the passage contains, so the count must be stated.
The model is asked for the first letter of the first line's character count when spelled out as a word; the count is required as an unspoken intermediate but never output.
Prompt positions at which a two-digit integer or a number-word appears among the top 3 tokens of the J-lens readout — the figure's marker for count content being present in the workspace there.
The three highest-ranked vocabulary tokens in the Jacobian lens readout of the residual stream at a given position; the shading threshold used in this figure.
The total number of shaded positions in that prompt — a one-number summary of how much count content the workspace carries under that question.

An intervention that exchanges one concept's J-lens coordinate for another's and holds the exchanged values fixed at every position and layer throughout the forward pass; here it rewrites every lens count in the forties to the matching value in the sixties.

The swap mapping: each two-digit lens token from 40 through 49 is replaced by the token 20 higher, so whatever count the workspace holds in the forties reads as the corresponding value in the sixties.
Task accuracy across the eleven passages: the model answers each of the three questions correctly on nearly every trial, so any difference between conditions is not a difference in competence.
How often count content appears in the lens under each condition: essentially zero under linewrap, moderate under explicit report, highest under the first-letter question.
Swap sensitivity: the answer follows the swapped lens value when the count is asked for or computed with, while the line-break decision under continuation is unaffected.
The example model answers to the direct character-count question: 46 naturally, 65 after the forties-to-sixties swap.

The example answers to the first-letter question: F for forty-six naturally, and S after the swap — the first letter of any count in the sixties, showing the swapped count was fed through the further computation.
The paper's candidate global workspace: the region of residual-stream space spanned by sparse nonnegative combinations of J-lens vectors, whose contents the lens readout reports.

numbers.meaning: Task conditions posed over the identical passage tokens: automatic linewrap, explicit report, and flexible computation (first letter of the count as a word).
The shading threshold: a token is shaded when a two-digit integer or number-word ranks in the top 3 of the J-lens readout at that position.
The swap mapping applied at every position: each lens count in the forties is replaced by the value 20 higher, so a workspace reading of 46 becomes 65.
The true character count of the example passage's first line, and the model's unmodified answer to the direct question.
The model's answer to the direct question after the swap — the swapped-in value, showing the reported count is read from the J-space rather than recomputed.
The number of prompt positions at which number tokens enter the lens top-3 under the explicit-report question in the example, against zero under the linewrap instruction on the same tokens.
Number tokens in the lens under the linewrap condition in the example: the count is being computed and used to place line breaks, yet none of it surfaces in the workspace.
The number of passages in the aggregate bottom row; each contributes all three conditions to panels (a), (b), and (c).
